same_witness_route.construction: Q is the canonical chart-coordinate subalgebra of the component field F; B is its integral closure in F; PB is the retained valuation center contracted to B. The ground-point output retains one maximal ideal M, residue equivalence eM, completion map Φ, parameter s, selected projective coordinates, and their two retained orders. The formally-etale core is checked under its stated hypotheses. The canonical axis-lift theorem chooses one α from its supplied formally-etale point, divisor/axis orders, and chart data. Common-open column and tangent consumers remain conditional on their stated maps, smoothness, closure, and derivative identities.

section_5_paper_statements.statement: Each statement of Section 5.2 has a Lean declaration with the paper's hypotheses and conclusion, and Theorem 5.7(i) is proved paragraph by paragraph from them.
section_5_paper_statements.module: Stafford38/Paper/Section5.lean (aggregator); Section5/Place.lean, ResidueBasis.lean, TangentCone.lean, GenericTangentRank.lean (lemmas); Section5/Steps.lean (paragraphs between the lemmas); Section5/Proof.lean (Theorem 5.7(i))

theorem_5_7.route: theorem_5_7_i_paper follows the printed proof: algebraic case (step_coordinate_algebraic); the discrete valuation ring of Lemmas 5.9-5.10 (Stafford38.Geometry.LaneC.divisorialVisibleFrameExistence calls lemma_5_9 and lemma_5_10); step_orders; step_generic_point; Lemma 5.11 (witness_lemma_5_11); step_dual_derivations; step_lambda_w_tau; step_M_minor; Lemma 5.12(a) bound (witness_lemma_5_12_5_13_paper, witness_lemma_5_12_a_bound); step_M_spans_cone (lemma_5_12_b, lemma_5_12_a_cone); step_lift_ell_minor; step_ell_conormal (lemma_5_13); step_polynomial_limit. The terminal theorem keeps the same-witness route of Stafford38.Geometry.GeneralAsymptoticConormal; both prove the same statement and both build their place with lemma_5_9 and lemma_5_10.

printed.scope: Stated for a nonempty, Zariski-closed, irreducible Y in K^n (Definition 5.4(a): Stafford38.Paper.Section5.IsIrreducibleClosed, equivalent to I(Y) prime by definition_5_4_a) with Y and H disjoint, and N(Y), Dir(Y) over the Jacobian smooth locus; derived from the prime-ideal forms theorem_5_7_i_prime and theorem_5_7_ii_prime with I(Y) = idealPoint Y. Theorem 5.8 applies theorem_5_7_i_printed to Y_0 = V_K(q) (step_theorem_5_7_applies).

section_5_paper_statements.witness_scope: The place of the formal proof is built by lemma_5_9 and lemma_5_10, with the column q_a = x̄_a / x̄_j for the chart j of lemma_5_9 (Stafford38.Geometry.LaneC.divisorialVisibleFrameExistenceWithChart), followed by a coefficient field E over which the residue field is finite (the input to the coefficient field of the completion, Matsumura Thm. 28.3), and keeps Lemma 5.10(c) (Stafford38.Geometry.GeneralDivisorialVisibleFrame.generalDivisorialVisibleFrameWithKaehlerFinite). The proof uses the printed constructions: a > 0 from Lemma 5.10(a) (step_a_pos, lemma_5_10_a_not_R_le), the unit minor M_iota (step_M_minor), the lift ell_iota = -u_upsilon M_upsilon M_iota^-1 (step_lift_ell_minor), and the bound m <= d'+1 of Lemma 5.12(a) by the second fundamental sequence and Nakayama (witness_lemma_5_12_a_bound).
